tools/generate_precomputed.py, so a preset cannot be defined in the app in
THE TWO MATCHED DATE PAIRS, per the model author's presentation:
1. The Precambrian-Cambrian boundary (~541 Ma) matched to the beginning
2. A conventional Ice Age endpoint (~12 ka) matched to the chronology's
K/Pg AND N/Q ARE NOT CALIBRATION INPUTS. They are competing Flood-boundary
models -- claims about where in the column Flood deposition ends. The
calibration does not depend on which is selected: each chronology gives one
curve, and the choice only asks where that curve puts the boundary. Testing
a Flood model means reading off where its boundary lands, which is what
Naming rule: a value ending in _age is an AGE (years before present), one
ending in _date is a DATE (years after Day 1 of Creation). The two run in
opposite directions; conflating them is a documented past bug in this
package, and the masoretic note below is exactly that hazard.

flood_start.label: Precambrian-Cambrian
flood_start.note: Pre-Flood/Flood contact, matched to the Flood's beginning.

ice_age_end.label: End of the Ice Age
ice_age_end.note: Conventional Ice Age endpoint, matched to the chronology's date.

masoretic.label: Masoretic
note: The package default (card.chronology.DEFAULT_CHRONOLOGY), in the
package's DATE convention: ice_age_end_date counts years AFTER
Creation, so the Ice Age ends at 2556 BP.
The author's presentation quotes 3500 years BEFORE present for the same
event. That is the same numeral read the other way round, and this
package's history records fitting at 3500 YBP rather than 2556 as a
bug -- so the DATE reading is used here deliberately.

septuagint.label: Septuagint (LXX)
note: PROVISIONAL. The Flood at 5324 BP is the author's figure. age_of_earth
is still a placeholder, and the Ice Age date is the author's 4200 BP
taken at face value -- unlike the Masoretic entry, which follows the
package default. The two chronologies are therefore NOT on the same
footing; this needs Rick's confirmation before publication.

nq.label: Neogene-Quaternary (N/Q)
nq.note: Flood deposition ends at 2.58 Ma (ICS) -- the late-Cenozoic option.

flood_only.label: Flood only
note: No Creation-week acceleration; an instantaneous onset at t_F relaxing
as a single exponential. t_F == t_F2.

general.label: Creation week + Flood
note: Authored but not exposed in v1. Turning this on is flipping `enabled`;
no component changes, because the parameter panel iterates the free
names Python returns rather than a hardcoded list.
Freeing lambda_c/k_c does not disturb the calibration: both constraint
ages map to formation DATEs at or after t_F, so their integrals cover
only the Flood and post-Flood regions and the Creation-week parameters
never enter. Verified to exactly zero difference.
Grid for the precomputed first-paint layer. Log-spaced in true age: the
structure is all in the recent end. Breakpoints, constraint ages and the
relaxation regions are unioned in by the generator.
